title: Walking a new site before the first shift
audience: New cleaners and supervisors taking on a site for the first time.
learningOutcomes: Locate the storage room, waste points and emergency contacts on a site walk-through.
Find the safety data sheets kept on site and explain what they are for.
Confirm the agreed task list and closing routine with the site contact before work starts.

instruction.heading: Why walk the site first
instruction.body: A walk-through turns an unfamiliar building into a map you can work from. Workers who skip it lose time searching for supplies, miss areas that sit out of normal sight lines, and learn the client's expectations only after something goes wrong. Walking the site with the person who manages it is the cheapest way to ask questions while there is still time to act on the answers.

instruction.heading: What to note on the way round
instruction.body: Record where supplies are stored and who holds the keys. Mark every waste point, including the ones tucked behind partitions or in rarely visited corridors. Note any switches, power points or hinges that carry a colour marker, because the markers often show where a surface is meant to be handled differently. Check where emergency numbers are posted and where the safety data sheets are kept, then read one sheet to see which sections cover handling and first aid. Finally, read the agreed task list and the closing routine, such as lights, doors and alarm.

instruction.heading: Turning notes into a working plan
instruction.body: Put your observations on a short site card and keep it with the job file. Any task that falls outside the agreed list should be marked as a question rather than a decision. Do not invent scope on the day. A short written message to the site contact keeps the record clear and protects both sides.

procedure: Book a walk-through with the site contact before the first shift.
Start at the storage room and note which supplies and equipment are held there.
Follow the path a worker would take through the site, marking waste points and trouble areas.
Locate emergency numbers, the first aid kit and the safety data sheets, and read the hazard section of one sheet.
Check the agreed task list and the closing routine with the site contact.
Complete the site card, list open questions, and file it with the job record.

workedExamples.situation: A three-storey office has a staff kitchen with no visible bin, and a lockable cupboard that the site contact says holds the cleaning products.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you record on the site card, and what do you ask before the first shift?
workedExamples.reasoning: Record the kitchen bin as a waste point and the cupboard as a product location to confirm. Ask whether the kitchen bin is in scope and whether the cupboard holds the products you plan to use. Find the safety data sheets for those products before using them. Every question is answered in writing before work begins.

equipmentAndPpe: Eye protection and gloves, worn as set for the site

commonErrors.error: Skipping the walk-through because the site looks simple or was cleaned before.
commonErrors.prevention: Walk every new site on the first visit, and again whenever the layout or scope changes.

commonErrors.error: Assuming the closing routine matches the last site worked.
commonErrors.prevention: Confirm the closing routine in writing and note it on the site card.

commonErrors.error: Opening a product without first locating its safety data sheet.
commonErrors.prevention: Locate the sheet during the walk-through and keep it where workers can reach it.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Safety data sheets must be easy to reach on site. Their location is part of the walk-through.
Duties under workplace health and safety law depend on the state or territory and on the model WHS laws. Specific duties must be checked before use.

qualityStandard: The site card lists the storage room, waste points, emergency numbers, safety data sheet location and closing routine.
Every open question is raised with the site contact before the first shift.
documentationEvidence: Completed site card, signed by the worker and the site contact.
Record of any task raised as outside the agreed list.
summary: A walk-through before the first shift saves time and prevents scope disputes.
Note supplies, waste points, emergency information and the closing routine.
Raise anything outside the agreed list in writing before acting on it.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the main purpose of a site walk-through before the first shift?
options: To learn where supplies, waste points and hazards are before work starts
To time a worker on a sample task and record the time taken for the task
To set the client's price for the job and the rate before the first shift

knowledgeChecks.question: During the walk-through you find a bin that is not on the agreed task list. What is the right first step?
options: Empty it, since bins are usually included in every walk-through
Record it on the site card and ask the site contact whether it is in scope
Leave it out of the notes so the walk-through finishes sooner

knowledgeChecks.question: Where should you look for handling and first aid details for a product on site?
options: The packaging of a similar product from the same range
The safety data sheet for that product, kept on site
A colleague's memory of the last site and the last visit
